evidence.observation: Menu card is up; Enter clears it into play.
evidence.riff: The start card states the contract before you touch anything: one jump, no double jump, unlimited retries.

evidence.observation: Right is held; the courier accelerates and the lamp wedge widens.
evidence.riff: Speed is a readout here — the widening cone is the running cue that does not depend on colour.

evidence.observation: One jump, fixed height, no double jump.
evidence.riff: Every landing downstream is built on this single unchanged number: a 56 px rise.

evidence.observation: Four jumps clear the starter's two gaps and its steps; geometry below x=960 is byte-identical.
evidence.riff: Leaving it untouched is what keeps the starter's own coyote, spike and fall fixtures valid as regression evidence.

evidence.observation: The courier jumps to clear the last spike; the spike springs up into the arc and kills it.
evidence.riff: Pure geometry: leaving the ground beside it is what arms it, so the naive play is the fatal one.

evidence.observation: Death card reads 'It goes up when you do'.
evidence.riff: The failure names its own cause, which is the difference between a trap and an ambush.

evidence.observation: About half a second later the run restarts at spawn with RETRIES 01.
evidence.riff: No lives and no menu: failure costs time, not progress — which is what makes a lethal trap acceptable.

evidence.observation: A 48 px up-jump onto ledge B, then hops to C and D.
evidence.riff: Measured takeoff windows 70, 56 and 58 px — chosen by probe, not by feel.

evidence.observation: A jump on ledge D takes the key; the HUD turns to KEY HELD.
evidence.riff: Standing on D the body occupies y 220–248 and the key spans 197–215, so walking under it is provably not enough.

evidence.observation: The key trails the courier as it turns and walks back.
evidence.riff: Carrying it visibly is what makes the door's demand legible before you reach the door.

evidence.observation: The ledge ends in a barrier marked DEAD END; the courier turns and drops back to the floor.
evidence.riff: The barrier is what converts a second route into a there-and-back errand — and it is why the level no longer asks you to choose.

evidence.observation: Running beneath the high ledges with WALK BACK / NO HEADROOM on the slab.
evidence.riff: A ceiling you cannot jump under is a cost you feel without being told twice.

evidence.observation: A 56 px gap cleared onto the merge platform.
evidence.riff: Measured takeoff window 38 px — the tightest required jump in the level.

evidence.observation: The courier stops short, hops straight up to spring the spike, then walks underneath it.
evidence.riff: The same input that kills you in the air is the one that clears the path from the ground.

evidence.observation: The key leaves the courier, flies to the lock and seats; LOCKED becomes OPEN.
evidence.riff: The dock line at x=1600 is the moment the errand pays off — the carried object becomes the thing that changes the level.

evidence.observation: The courier walks into the open door; Course complete.
evidence.riff: The finish moved from a flag at 916 to a door at 1696, and it will not accept you without the key.

evidence.observation: Enter on the completion card starts a fresh session; retries reset and the key is restored.
evidence.riff: Replay re-locks the door and re-arms the trap, so a second run is a real second run.

evidence.observation: Escape raises the pause card and freezes the run; Enter resumes from the same position.
evidence.riff: Pause freezes the clock as well as the player, which is why the finish time stays meaningful.

evidence.observation: R restarts the attempt from spawn and the retry counter stays at 00.
evidence.riff: Choosing to restart is not failing, and the counter agrees.

evidence.observation: The HUD switches from KEY -- to KEY HELD, and the progress bar tracks spawn to door.
evidence.riff: The bar is derived from level data; the starter divided by a hard-coded 852 and saturated less than halfway along this level.
